card.title: Before I Knew Better
card.instruction: Perform the more hopeful version of yourself from before disappointment taught you caution, and defend that version when reality intrudes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've written when our shop opens. Before the first one failed, I never wrote if.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't afford another empty opening party.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll bake. I used to assume people would come for my cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six generous portions. I'm writing 'come early' on the invitations.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 restores pre-failure when rather than if, A3 revives faith in cake attendance, and A5 turns a six-portion limit into confident come-early invitations.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's empty-party cost concern makes A3 offer baking; B4's portion budget becomes A5's optimistic scarcity framing.

relationship.evidence: B2 remembers the failed opening and B4 sets an actual affordable quantity.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's small budget as a reason to expect demand rather than revert to caution.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a prior failed shop and a proposed new opening; B2-B4 define the catering constraint.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's come-early wording develops B4's six portions and A1's deliberate hopeful language.

coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect; present constraints shape rather than erase the performed hopeful self.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 embraces B4's limit through generous portions and anticipated demand.
